cards.title: Optimize Collection Pages Without Pushing Products Down
cards.summary: Add keyword-rich collection titles and descriptions while keeping the product grid above the fold.
cards.use_when: Improving a collection page (e.g., 'Bath') that currently has no descriptive content.

cards.title: Optimize Pages and Blog Posts, Then Interlink Them
cards.summary: Apply the same title/description/handle process to all pages and posts, and build internal links to spread crawl coverage.
cards.use_when: Extending SEO beyond products and collections, and setting up internal linking between blog content and products.

cards.title: Mobile-Friendliness and Page Speed Checks for Ranking
cards.summary: Verify mobile rendering and diagnose load-speed issues Google uses to rank stores.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme before or after launch for mobile and speed problems that suppress rankings.

cards.title: Add Rich Snippets (FAQ and Product Schema)
cards.summary: Enable structured data so search results show FAQs, ratings, prices, and availability.
cards.use_when: Wanting extra visible SERP real estate for product, FAQ, or article content.

cards.title: Submit the Shopify XML Sitemap to Search Console
cards.summary: Point Google at your sitemap after setting your primary domain.
cards.use_when: Finalizing technical SEO setup after optimizing pages so Google can crawl and index them.

cards.title: Set Brand Information for Search and Sales Channels
cards.summary: Fill in the Shopify brand tab so Google, Facebook, and other channels represent you accurately.
cards.use_when: Setting up or refreshing store branding that feeds external sales channels and search appearances.

cards.title: Build Backlinks and Recurring Content for Authority
cards.summary: Grow authority through external links and consistent publishing, which the source frames as what Google rewards.
cards.use_when: Planning off-page SEO and content cadence to lift overall ranking potential.

cards.title: Audit Existing Rankings to Fix Wasted Content
cards.summary: Review which keywords you already rank for and correct pages ranking for irrelevant or zero-volume terms.
cards.use_when: Doing a periodic SEO review to redirect content toward terms that actually drive traffic.

cards.title: Deciding Whether to Automate Shopify SEO with an App
cards.summary: Weigh manual on-page SEO against app-based automation for image compression, scores, snippets, and keyword research.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to execute SEO at scale across a large catalog.

cards.title: Deciding whether SEO is worth pursuing for a Shopify store
cards.summary: A pre-investment filter for judging if organic search can become a profitable channel or a waste of months.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest budget, time or agency fees into SEO for your store, before writing any content.

cards.title: Capturing branded search your paid ads create
cards.summary: Paid awareness generates branded searches that a competitor may capture if you don't rank for your own name.
cards.use_when: Planning paid acquisition or auditing whether competitors outrank you on your own brand and category terms.

cards.title: Multiplying collection pages to target keyword variations
cards.summary: Replace one broad collection page with many specific sub-collection pages that reuse the same products.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a product category where you currently have a single broad collection page competing on one high-difficulty term.

cards.title: The four blog formats that still drive ecommerce revenue
cards.summary: Replace lifestyle and seasonal blog content with four bottom- and mid-funnel formats built for buyer intent.
cards.use_when: Planning a content calendar or auditing existing blog posts that get traffic but no sales.

cards.title: Building an internal linking system that funnels authority to money pages
cards.summary: Use controlled internal links to push SEO value and user flow toward collection and product pages that convert.
cards.use_when: Optimising an existing store with orphaned blog posts and product pages that never get internal links.

cards.title: Getting cited in AI search results (GEO)
cards.summary: Structure product and content pages with high specificity so AI tools quote your store in generated answers.
cards.use_when: Adapting your PDPs, collections and content for AI Overviews, Perplexity or ChatGPT-style answers that bypass the ten blue links.

cards.title: Research conversational and long-tail queries for AI-driven search
cards.summary: Start GEO work by finding the conversational, question-shaped, long-tail queries users actually type into AI engines rather than head keywords.
cards.use_when: Planning product-page copy, category descriptions, or blog topics so the store can surface in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews answers.

cards.title: Write direct, answer-first content instead of keyword-density fluff
cards.summary: GEO content should clearly and contextually answer a specific question rather than stuff keywords into long generic pieces.
cards.use_when: Writing PDP copy, buying guides, or FAQ content intended to be cited by AI engines.

cards.title: Structure and schema-model pages for AI parsing
cards.summary: Well-structured pages with clear headings, lists, and schema markup are easier for AI engines to extract and reuse.
cards.use_when: Formatting PDPs, category pages, or guides, or when adding structured data for schedules, reviews, or pricing.

cards.title: Match content to user intent across the funnel
cards.summary: Prioritize what the user actually wants to know, covering informational through transactional intent to widen the chance an AI engine features you.
cards.use_when: Deciding which pages to create or rewrite so both research-stage and buy-stage queries can surface your store.

cards.title: Use reviews, testimonials and UGC as fresh AI-visible content
cards.summary: Distributing content socially and encouraging customer reviews and UGC adds authenticity and diverse perspectives that AI engines are said to value.
cards.use_when: Building review collection, social distribution, or on-site UGC for a product to improve both trust and AI visibility.

cards.title: Build answer authority with citations, experts and statistics
cards.summary: Supporting content with reliable references, expert quotes, and relevant statistics builds trust with both users and AI algorithms.
cards.use_when: Writing category guides, buying advice, or health/specialty product content where credibility affects citation and conversion.

cards.title: Treat GEO as an ongoing monitoring and adaptation loop
cards.summary: Generative engine optimization is not one-time work; you must watch how AI platforms evolve and keep refining content.
cards.use_when: Setting a recurring workstream for AI search visibility alongside SEO analytics and rank tracking.

cards.title: Keyword vetting with the BID formula
cards.summary: Screen candidate keywords through business potential, SERP intent match and ranking difficulty before committing content budget.
cards.use_when: Product selection and content planning: deciding which keyword clusters to build category, product or comparison pages around for an online store.

cards.title: AI filter: avoid keywords AI already fully answers
cards.summary: Before targeting a keyword, judge whether an AI overview satisfies the searcher so completely that no click will happen.
cards.use_when: Content prioritisation for a store blog or buying guide where you would otherwise invest in informational posts that never earn clicks.

cards.title: Find competitor mention gaps with branded-query filters
cards.summary: Use AI visibility tooling to isolate prompts where competitors are named but your brand is absent, especially best/top/versus/review/alternative queries.
cards.use_when: Competitive positioning and merchandising decisions about which comparison and best-of content to produce so your store gets named in AI answers.

cards.title: Content structure: BLUF, atomic sections, entities, declarative sentences
cards.summary: Four writing rules that let both skimming humans and chunking LLMs extract your key answer from any section of a PDP-supporting article or guide.
cards.use_when: Writing or editing buying guides, category explainers and comparison articles on a store's content hub.

cards.title: Content length, freshness and format signals for AI citations
cards.summary: Cited pages are not long, are meaningfully fresher than organic results, and skew heavily toward lists and comparisons — so refresh and format beat word count.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to rewrite or expand category and guide pages, and choosing which content formats to invest in for AI visibility.

cards.title: Refresh sleeper pages to win citations fastest
cards.summary: Find pages with backlinks but declining traffic and update them, because existing authority plus refreshed content is the quickest route to AI citations.
cards.use_when: Replenishment of an existing content library: choosing which product guides or category pages to update this quarter instead of writing new ones.

cards.title: Brand the frameworks you invent to resist LLM flattening
cards.summary: Name original concepts after your brand and distribute them widely so AI credits rather than absorbs them as generic knowledge.
cards.use_when: Differentiating your store's expertise — sizing systems, fit guides, material standards or comparison frameworks — in a market where AI summarises everything.

cards.title: Tier-one mentions: get listed on editorial listicles and comparison pages
cards.summary: Prioritise mentions in authoritative third-party editorial content, which correlate most strongly with AI overview visibility, and locate the target pages programmatically.
cards.use_when: Acquisition and brand-building for a store trying to be named in AI answers to best-of and versus queries in its product category.

cards.title: Tier-two mentions on community and UGC platforms, without spamming
cards.summary: Reddit, Quora and niche forums are heavily cited and foundational training sources, but the source warns against dropping your brand name into threads.
cards.use_when: Community-led visibility for a store whose buyers research in forums and subreddits before purchasing.

cards.title: Query fan-out and why topical coverage beats single-keyword pages
cards.summary: AI expands one prompt into many synthetic sub-queries, so pages must cover a whole topic rather than one exact match keyword.
cards.use_when: Category page and buying-guide planning for a store that wants to be pulled into AI answers about its product area.

cards.title: AI visibility is probabilistic, not a ranking position
cards.summary: Citations vary between identical prompts and are shaped by consensus, freshness and authority, so track share of visibility rather than a fixed rank.
cards.use_when: Setting expectations and KPIs for a store's AI search programme before investing in content or mentions.

cards.title: Two information sources: training data vs real-time retrieval
cards.summary: AI answers come from static training snapshots or live web retrieval (RAG), giving you two distinct levers — broad mentions and crawlable, rankable content.
cards.use_when: Planning how a new product launch or store brand will be discovered in AI assistants within weeks rather than months.

cards.title: Check CDN and robots rules for accidental search-crawler blocking
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.

cards.title: Capture AI-driven demand with a post-purchase 'how did you hear about us?' survey
cards.summary: Unlinked AI mentions arrive as 'Direct' traffic, so self-reported attribution is needed to see the brand awareness AI generates.
cards.use_when: Attribution and retention analytics for a store whose AI mentions often come without links.

cards.title: Diagnose visibility gaps across six dimensions
cards.summary: A six-bucket framework — visibility, narrative, topic, format, web mentions and demand — turns AI visibility data into a prioritised action list.
cards.use_when: Quarterly planning for a store's content and brand programme, deciding whether to fix, build or influence.

cards.title: Platform-specific citation preferences: where to allocate AEO effort
cards.summary: AI platforms barely overlap in sources, so match your existing strengths and target sources to the specific engine you prioritise.
cards.use_when: Channel prioritisation: choosing whether to invest in YouTube, editorial PR, community presence or traditional rankings based on which AI engine your category's buyers use.

cards.title: Treat AI visibility as a spectrum: cited, mentioned, or invisible
cards.summary: Three states of AI visibility, each with different business value, so define which state matters for your store before optimising.
cards.use_when: Goal-setting and reporting for an AI search programme, and choosing whether to chase links, mentions or both.

cards.title: Mining listicles and comparisons where your brand is absent
cards.summary: Find high-authority listicle and comparison pages in your niche that omit your brand, then pursue mentions there because AI pulls from those pages.
cards.use_when: Planning a link/mention acquisition campaign to increase AI citations for your product category.

cards.title: Earning mentions in community and UGC platforms
cards.summary: Join and contribute genuinely to Reddit, Quora, and niche forums where your buyers ask questions, because these are heavily cited and used as AI training sources.
cards.use_when: Building brand visibility on community platforms to influence AI recommendations for your product category.

cards.title: Using owned content properties as additional AI citation sources
cards.summary: Leverage your own owned channels (secondary domains, YouTube, podcast, social) as topically relevant citation sources that AI can learn from.
cards.use_when: Deciding which owned channels to invest in to increase your brand's presence in AI training and citation data.

cards.title: Running a regular brand mention audit
cards.summary: Periodically audit whether your brand mentions and AI sentiment have changed, because pages get updated and your brand can be added or removed without notice.
cards.use_when: Monitoring and maintaining your store's brand reputation in AI-generated answers and cited sources over time.

cards.title: Targeting search-hit YouTube topics instead of viral hits
cards.summary: Prioritize YouTube topics with sustained search demand over viral ones because search hits get consistent traffic and are more likely to be cited by AI.
cards.use_when: Planning a YouTube content calendar to drive durable product discovery through both Google and AI answers.

cards.title: YouTube video ranking checklist for product discovery
cards.summary: Five on-video elements that make a video rank in Google and get cited by AI, from title keywords to spoken terms and format matching.
cards.use_when: Producing YouTube videos intended to surface in search and AI answers for product-relevant queries.

cards.title: Finding YouTube topics AI is already citing for your niche
cards.summary: Use a brand-tracking topics report filtered to youtube.com to find queries where AI pulls YouTube videos, then create content for those topics.
cards.use_when: Deciding which YouTube topics to produce to maximize probability of AI citation.

cards.title: Audit search crawler access independently from training permissions
cards.summary: Verify public product and collection pages are accessible to the intended search crawlers while preserving separate training choices.
cards.use_when: A store wants product pages discoverable in AI search or is diagnosing missing product visibility after CDN or theme changes.

cards.title: Handling JavaScript rendering and page speed for AI crawlers
cards.summary: Some AI crawlers can't render JavaScript and drop slow pages during real-time retrieval, so serve server-rendered, fast pages.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a store's key pages aren't being read or cited by ChatGPT and other AI crawlers.

cards.title: Structuring HTML for AI parsability
cards.summary: Logical heading hierarchy and self-contained sections make it easier for AI systems to chunk and extract the right content from your pages.
cards.use_when: Building or editing product pages, category pages, or blog posts so AI can cleanly extract and cite their content.

cards.title: Using and limiting schema markup for AEO
cards.summary: Schema markup is low-risk but unproven for AI citation; add standard types as a good habit without over-investing for AEO alone.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much time to spend on structured data when setting up new store pages.

cards.title: Capturing traffic from AI-hallucinated 404 URLs
cards.summary: AI assistants send users to nonexistent pages more often than Google does; catch that traffic by redirecting hallucinated URLs to relevant real pages.
cards.use_when: Recovering lost store traffic that clicks AI-recommended links to pages that don't exist.

cards.title: Setting up an AI traffic channel group in GA4
cards.summary: Isolate AI referral traffic in GA4 with a custom channel group so you can see which platforms and pages AI sends visitors to.
cards.use_when: Measuring whether AI assistants are driving measurable referral traffic to your store.

cards.title: Tracking AI bot activity to identify citation candidates
cards.summary: Monitor the AI crawlers visiting your site to find which pages AI is paying attention to and which are underexplored by bots.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing which store pages are strong AI citation candidates and which are hidden from crawlers.

cards.title: Capturing AI impact through self-reported attribution
cards.summary: Survey customers on how they heard about you to capture AI-influenced conversions that appear as direct or branded organic traffic.
cards.use_when: Attributing conversions to AI visibility when analytics can't show the AI touchpoint for your store.

cards.title: Combining three tracking pillars for AI visibility
cards.summary: No single AI measurement source is complete; combine referral traffic, bot analytics, and self-reported attribution to see the full picture.
cards.use_when: Setting up an ongoing AEO measurement framework for an online store.

cards.title: Prioritizing and evaluating AI traffic volume vs. quality
cards.summary: AI referral traffic is small in volume but high in intent and conversion quality, and its growth trajectory argues for starting early.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether an AEO program is worth investing in for the store, and how to frame its ROI.

cards.title: Filling information gaps to resist AI misinformation
cards.summary: AI repeats fake or outdated brand info when official, specific content is missing; publish authoritative FAQs and facts to reduce the risk.
cards.use_when: Protecting an online store's brand accuracy in AI answers and reducing the chance AI cites false claims about your products or pricing.

cards.title: Completing a monthly and quarterly brand radar check
cards.summary: Track four AI visibility metrics monthly and do a deeper competitive audit quarterly to know if your AEO efforts are working.
cards.use_when: Reviewing whether content, mention-earning, and video efforts are improving the store's AI visibility.

cards.title: Executing a starter AEO action plan this week
cards.summary: A five-step first week of AEO work: fix crawler access, set up AI analytics, refresh key pages, run a brand gap analysis, and pick top mention targets.
cards.use_when: Kicking off an AEO program for an online store with no prior structured AI visibility work.

cards.title: Query fan-out: optimize for the sub-queries AI actually runs
cards.summary: AI assistants expand one user prompt into several background searches, so visibility depends on ranking for those sub-queries, not the original prompt.
cards.use_when: Planning which product, category and landing pages to build or optimize so an AI assistant can surface the store for high-intent shopping prompts.

cards.title: Why scaled AI content is a rank-and-tank risk
cards.summary: Mass-producing AI articles to chase fan-out variations creates a short traffic spike followed by a collapse, and the source argues recovery can take years.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to accept a vendor's or in-house plan to scale the store's blog from hundreds to thousands of posts for AI visibility.

cards.title: Audit a scaled-content case study with keyword difficulty
cards.summary: Aggregate traffic charts can hide a decline in the hard, commercially valuable keywords, so analyze difficulty bands separately.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a GEO agency's or tool's case study before signing, or auditing whether your own scaled content push is actually holding up.

cards.title: Red flags and yellow flags when vetting a GEO vendor
cards.summary: Screen AI-visibility vendors by whether their platform generates content at scale and by what they actually propose doing off-site.
cards.use_when: Choosing or renewing an agency/tool that promises to improve the store's visibility inside AI assistants.

cards.title: The five questions to ask a GEO vendor before hiring
cards.summary: A concrete question set that surfaces whether an AI-visibility vendor has durable experience or is selling scaled-content tactics.
cards.use_when: Running a sales call or RFP with an agency or platform pitching AI search visibility for your store.

cards.title: Correct persistent inaccurate brand facts across public sources
cards.summary: Repeatedly restating a corrected fact on your own site and across distributed channels can shift what a model says even without a web search.
cards.use_when: When an AI assistant keeps repeating an outdated or misleading fact about your store — e.g. shipping times, return policy, product capabilities, implementation or lead times.

cards.title: Distinguish observed web retrieval from unverified answer provenance
cards.summary: Run the same query in free/incognito and logged-in/paid sessions and inspect citations to see whether the assistant searched the web at all.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in training-data/brand work or web-page optimization for a given set of shopping or brand prompts.

cards.title: Prompt trackers: understand their limits before trusting AI visibility data
cards.summary: Automated AI prompt trackers can report inflated or meaningless visibility when answers vary run-to-run or the model never searched the web.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report from a tool, agency or in-house dashboard to decide whether the store is actually being recommended.

cards.title: Verify claimed Reddit influence before paying for Reddit GEO
cards.summary: Test which Reddit threads actually influence the prompts you care about — often none you can join, and some are locked.
cards.use_when: Being pitched a Reddit-mentions service for your store, or considering building a Reddit presence for AI visibility.

cards.title: Get listed in the third-party listicles AI already cites
cards.summary: Find the affiliate review pages and listicles that influence your priority prompts and get your brand placed in those, not in new ones you create.
cards.use_when: Building off-site AI visibility for a store in a category where comparison listicles (supplements, mattresses, credit cards, fragrances, software) drive AI answers.

cards.title: Rank category and product pages for bottom-of-funnel queries without building listicles
cards.summary: Your own category and product pages can capture high-intent queries and get cited by AI, without any third-party placement.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to build next on-site for AI visibility — a new blog post or an optimized commercial page.

cards.title: Treat GEO as a company-wide function, not a single marketing hire
cards.summary: Because AI answers draw on product quality, reviews, PR, social and support channels, one person cannot fix AI visibility alone.
cards.use_when: Scoping who owns AI search performance at your store and setting cross-team responsibilities.

cards.title: Investigate stale brand facts and correct likely public sources
cards.summary: When a model answers about your brand without searching, it is drawing on sources like G2, Reddit or directories — correct those sources directly.
cards.use_when: An AI assistant gives an outdated answer about your store's policies, pricing, product capabilities or review sentiment without performing a web search.

cards.title: Test whether an AI answer is naming your brand or only linking your page
cards.summary: A citation is not the same as a mention — being linked while a competitor is named is not a win for the store.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an AI visibility report or checking a Google AI overview for your category to judge whether the visibility claimed is worth anything.

cards.title: Judge AI-visibility tactics by whether they optimize for the user's best answer
cards.summary: The durable test for any GEO tactic is whether it improves the experience of searchers, not whether it produces a spike in tracked mentions.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to adopt a specific AI-visibility tactic — self-authored listicles, scaled comparison pages, paid placements — for your store.

cards.title: Bottom-of-funnel pages beat top-of-funnel content for AI citation
cards.summary: Build specific, high-intent scenario and service pages rather than broad informational content that AI already answers itself.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend limited content budget on a store's blog versus category/product/scenario pages.

cards.title: Mine query fan-out language to write on-site copy
cards.summary: Inspect the actual searches an LLM runs, then reuse that exact phrasing in page titles, slugs, H1s and first sentences.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a product, category or landing page's on-page text so the store surfaces in AI-run web searches.

cards.title: Cheap press releases to influence AI answers
cards.summary: Use low-cost newswire distributions with your target phrase repeated in the title, subheading and first sentence to get cited by AI.
cards.use_when: Building brand impressions or correcting/creating an AI-visible narrative about a product, store or founder.

cards.title: Publish pricing intent to control AI answers about cost
cards.summary: State your pricing or a starting-from figure on your site so AI doesn't invent a number from G2 or Reddit.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to hide pricing on a B2B or high-ticket product page and what to publish instead.

cards.title: Optimize reviews across every platform, not just one
cards.summary: Diversify and monitor your review presence everywhere AI looks, because any single platform can drop out of AI results.
cards.use_when: Managing review profiles and reputation for a store that relies on third-party review sites for AI-driven product comparisons.

cards.title: Disclose useful product info on-site so AI doesn't guess
cards.summary: Put pricing, specs and positioning on your own pages so third parties don't define your product in AI answers.
cards.use_when: Deciding what product details to publish versus hide, to control how AI describes your store and products.
